utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Anttila, I think we have to deal with a few procedural matters so if you will have a bit of patience. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I would just like to suggest that Exhibit D133, which was introduced into the private session should be admitted under the seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, is that on the record, that D133, as the Chamber now decides, is admitted under seal. Yes. That's confirmed. If there's no other matter, good morning again, Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence in this court the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to stand and to make that solemn declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Anttila. Please be seated. English is not your native language. If you have ever any problem either in understanding or in expressing yourself in that language, please address me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, could you please state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: My full name is Kari Juhami Anttila.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you recall giving four statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in connection with this case?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your permission I'd like to provide the witness with paper copies of his statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, taking a look at those, can you tell us whether those are the statements that you made to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And to be clear, the statement of 18 December of 1995, that is 65 ter 4774, the statement dated 8 January 1996, is 65 ter number 1052. The statement dated 16 October 1997, is 65 ter number 4804, and the final statement dated 12 December 2007 is 65 ter number 4805. Now, Mr. Anttila, did you have a chance to review all of those statements prior to coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether the information contained in each of those statements is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And do those statements, do each of them accurately reflect what you said?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if asked the same questions here in court today, would your answers be the same as in those statements?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move for the admission of each of these statements and I can repeat the 65 ter numbers if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that 1052?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That was the 8 January 1996 statement, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I may just -- but let's start with the first one. I think we start with 4774.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 18th of December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you'll recall that's the same statement as Mr. Munkelien.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's P60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I wasn't sure how the court would prefer to proceed. I thought it would be best to have this in addition to since it is a statement of both of them but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if the one is in evidence and if the witness here now testifies that he would give the same answers and that the statement is to the best of his knowledge in accordance with the truth, then I think there's no need to have it admitted again. So that P60 is the 18th of December statement. Let me just check one second. Yes. Then the next one would be P1052. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's true for all the Defence teams. Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P171, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P171 is admitted into evidence. The next one is P4804. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is the October '07 -- excuse me, 1997. No objection. Obviously, Your Honour, my objection is with regard to admissibility and not to weight, but when I say no objection it's on the admissibility score.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the October 1997 statement would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P172, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just correct it. I mean I think -- I don't know if I misspoke. I said my objection is not with regard to admissibility, but I obviously the issue that I take -- to the extent I take issue it's to weight, but I do believe that either I misspoke or it was written incorrectly in the prior transcript at line 25 going into line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said my objection is with regard to admissibility, not to weight, it was just the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P172, since there are no objections, is admitted into evidence. Then 4805. That is the -- that is the 12th of December, 2007. No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I take it you've spoken for all Defence teams, Mr. Kehoe. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P173.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And P173 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Russo, am I mistaken when I said that there was another statement as well but you do not tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You are not mistaken, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. At this time I'd request permission to read a brief summary of the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Anttila is informed about the procedure that -- Mr. Anttila, it's for the public to know what is in all these statements that are admitted into evidence, that a brief summary will be read. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Anttila was a United Nations military observer assigned to Team Podkonje in Sector South from 14 August until 27 November of 1995. Mr. Anttila participated in assessing the damage in Knin caused by shelling operations, burning and looting, and also performed a crater analysis of six impacts from a 128-millimetre multiple barrel rocket launcher system in a residential area of Knin. Mr. Anttila sometimes performed the functions of the duty or operations officer for the UNMO teams and on occasion drafted UNMO sitreps either for his UNMO Team Podkonje or for the UNMO HQ in Sector South. In addition to his responsibilities as an UNMO, Mr. Anttila also participated in patrols as part of the Human Rights Action Teams in Sector South. He was also tasked to prepare summaries of the humanitarian violations reported by the UNMO teams in their daily sitreps and to create reports detailing the information collected during the comprehensive damage survey conducted by all UNMO teams in Sector South which recorded the number of houses destroyed or damaged in over 400 villages in the Krajina. That concludes the summary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up Exhibit P64, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking at Exhibit P64, can you tell me if you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And did you participate in the damage assessment upon which this report is based?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I -- excuse me. I participated on that one during that day, and there were also other people who were taking part in that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And who were those other people? Were they members of your UNMO team?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: They were members of the UNMO Team Podkonje.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain how the assignment to conduct this damage survey came about?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, on that day we were -- for myself we were tasked to -- to conduct the crater analysis on those rocket impacts in the -- in the area, and while we were doing that we were going through the area, driving through the residential area and doing the assessment along the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Court where the -- the assignment came from to conduct that assessment?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That came from the SMO, the senior military observer of the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did the senior military observer give you this assignment verbally or was it in writing?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: In that case it was given verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could please just briefly explain to the Court exactly how the assessment was carried out by yourself as well as your fellow UNMO team members.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The assessment was carried out in a way that we left from the sector headquarters. We drove by car to the locations which each of the teams were assigned to, and we were assigned to go to -- to that certain residential area to collect the information about the impacts, and on the way we did not go directly to that area. We were going through the parts of the town where there were residential buildings. So -- so we -- we went there directly without any hesitation and any waiting, but we went through some areas where -- where things could be observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how long did this damage assessment take on that day?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: For myself and for the part of tour, what we did was -- it was an afternoon task so it took a few hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And do you know how long the other members of your UNMO team took to conduct their portions of this damage assessment?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, they also had only that afternoon to -- to conduct the -- the survey originally tasked to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up -- I believe it is P62. Thank you. And if we could please just enlarge the sort of middle downtown section. That's fine. Thank you. And, Your Honours, if I could please ask for the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, could you please mark or circle the areas where UNMO Team Podkonje searched for the damage on the afternoon of 17 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. Myself and Mr. Munkelien, we were around about that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: And the other -- I think it was -- at the time it was three different patrols who were going around this area in -- in general this area, and about this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you could please just next to each one of those circles mark the letters PA?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: PA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: PA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I -- just to making it clear, could we have a different designation for the particular area that Mr. Anttila looked at, so when we're looking at this down the line we have the other areas and then the specific area that Mr. Munkelien and Mr. Anttila looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. That's a good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Why don't we please if you could mark the area where yourself and Mr. Munkelien searched as A, and mark the other areas where the other teams searched as B, C, and D.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes. The B is not easily.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make the B even better? There's a way of removing what you've written. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please make the B --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And at the time you conducted this damage survey what was your understanding of what the military targets in the town were?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The only military target that I was aware of was the north -- what we called north barracks in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you could, please, place a circle around that area you're talking about and mark that as E.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did the other members of Team Podkonje indicate to you or consider during this provisional assessment any other locations in Knin that they considered to be military targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move for admission of this marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P174 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could just have one additional copy of P62 brought up. And if we can also focus again on the same area. And once again if we could just briefly have the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, you indicated that you performed a crater analysis also on this day. Can you please circle the location where yourself and Mr. Munkelien performed that crater analysis.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move to have this admitted as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I guess I need some degree of clarity, Your Honour, from the standpoint of is this different from what we had as A the area where he searched. It seems to me, and I may be mistaken, but it looks like exactly same.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you search the same area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness says the area he marked A, although is this the same size? Is it larger or is it smaller. I would have to compare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be my hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we're talking about a crater which is of the size of perhaps one or two metres. Then of course we have a few streets here so it doesn't add anything. It was within the area given the letter A in the previous exhibit. Therefore, Mr. Russo, does it add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, it doesn't add anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think it's of no great use to have this admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you withdraw tendering it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We no long are require the assistance the court usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And just to confirm, Mr. Anttila, as the Court indicated, the area that you marked as A in the last exhibit, that is also the area where you conducted the crater analysis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back to the provisional assessment, was there any record made during that assessment of -- other than the crater analysis which you just mentioned, was there any record made of the exact locations of every shell impact that was found on the afternoon of 17 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And to whom did Team Podkonje report the findings of that provisional assessment on that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We reported all the findings directly to the SMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was that at a briefing? Was it in a report? How did you do that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Basically it was in the briefing after the afternoon patrols had come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And how did you indicate to the senior military observer the areas where you found the damage?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We were indicating them by pointing them out on the map in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is there -- was there map in an office or --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Or -- okay. That was the operations office of the UNMO headquarter Sector South, and there was of course a map of the area on the -- on the wall. So these -- these areas that were covered were indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did you do that simply by pointing to the areas?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the UNMOs during this afternoon search of Knin, did they collect any information on the damage done to the military targets themselves?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, we were not allowed to enter the north barracks, so we could not assess any damages inside that area, and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if we could please, Madam Registrar, bring P64 up again. And if we could turn, please, to the second page and focus on paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking at paragraph 7, if you can see where it indicates that: "The survey continues to get a more accurate picture and better assessment. Detailed report to follow within a week." To your knowledge was there a detailed report that followed within one week?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And referring to your statement of 8 January 1996 you indicate that you found more areas where shells had landed and it was obvious from these later observations that the shelling did not concentrate on military targets --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I object to leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm simply directing him to the portion of his statement where this information is contained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you then perhaps point to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That would be paragraph 3 of the 8 January 1996 statement, which is now Exhibit P171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can ask the witness to read for himself the paragraph first and then put questions to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, referring -- if you could look at paragraph 3 of your 8 January 1996 statement.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The first sentence of that statement where it says that it was possible to find out more locations where artillery and mortar shells and rockets had landed, does that mean that you found more damage than was originally reported in the provisional assessment?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether or not some of that damage was located in the same areas where Team Podkonje searched on the 17th of August?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was some of that damage found in areas which were not in the close vicinity of military targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, these findings were found out in areas which I just pointed out, which were in a way driven through during the provisional assessment, and then later on when the debris and everything was cleared out you could find out impacts of -- of shelling later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, you are aware that your question suggests a common understanding of the military targets, where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I take it then is this limited to what the witness said before, northern barracks or --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could clarify that for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And looking at your 8 January 1996 statement, again at paragraph 3, Mr. Anttila, where it says: "Craters could be found clearly in residential areas and also in first assessment factories, et cetera, were considered military objectives. This cannot be confirmed afterwards." Earlier you indicated that the only military target which was considered at the time was the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: This makes reference to factories, et cetera. Can you tell me, were there additional facilities other than the northern barracks which were considered military objectives for purposes of the provisional assessment itself?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. Having been in the area for just a couple of days, not everything was clear when we were making the provisional assessment. Later on those few production facilities within the area of downtown Knin were sometimes referred as military compounds or whatever, and then later on we had discussions about whether they were of that nature and -- and anyway, the point is that with the crater I'm -- I was referring to the crater analysis conducted on the 17th of August while writing this down, and that at that time the closest military objective was the north barracks, and no matter which of those later may be considered to -- to be military objectives, they would not be any closer than the north barracks to the area where the rocket impacts had landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please again pull up the aerial photograph P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking again at the aerial photograph of Knin. You've already indicated where the northern barracks was. I'd like you to please indicate where the factories, et cetera, that you reference in your 8 January 1996 statement.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were there any other facilities that you indicated that you had discussions with your fellow UNMO team members that they thought were military targets at the time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. So anyway, the case is the area of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And so these two facilities, in addition to the northern barracks, were there any other facilities considered by UNMO Team Podkonje to have been military targets in Knin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would object to the comment about what Team Podkonje thought was military targets, because as you see from the provisional assessment, it was written by the SMO with quite a different tilt. Now, if what the witness wants to talk about he considered to be military targets, that's a different subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood your testimony. When you're talking about military targets, you're -- as a matter of fact, as the witness explained were the potential military targets he discussed with his colleagues as -- that's well understood. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have this exhibit, please, marked as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we had the -- I think the first -- let me just check. The first marking was about the factories, isn't it? Could you please put an F to the first circle you put there, and an M for the other one, which is what you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which is a compound of -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you considered it possibly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were discussing about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you were discussing about this as a military target.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether it was a military target or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's understood. Then you want to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections? No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exhibit P175 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, madam court usher. I think we're done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, other than the locations which you've indicated on this map and on the previous map as military targets, in your subsequent patrols through Knin did you find shelling impacts in areas not close to any of those areas?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court whether or not you found more than five impacts in those areas not close to any of the military targets you've indicated?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was the senior military observer made aware of the fact that you found additional damage in areas not close to these military targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And was there any discussion amongst your team regarding the accuracy of the provisional assessment?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, there was, so to say, in front of him and also when he was not present with the discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And to your knowledge did the senior military observer ever produce a follow-up report indicating that the provisional assessment report was subsequently found to be inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: In terms of saying that the provisional assessment was inaccurate in terms of being too low or -- or anything like that, I don't know anything about that kind of report, but the fact is that based on these first findings we were tasked to make the survey on the whole sector, and that led into the reports that have been taken into evidence later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And along with what you've just mentioned, if --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up Exhibit P63.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, taking a look at Exhibit P63, can you tell me if this is what you just made reference to?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you can recall when exactly it was that this document was drafted. Was it given to you before you conducted the provisional assessment or sometime afterwards?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, you can see on the date and group on the top that we were probably out doing the actual crater analysis when it was sent out. So this was done the same day but after provisional assessment teams were sent out, and that's simultaneous action that was taken by SMO, and this was sent to other teams within the AOR, and at that time the Podkonje or -- or the people in Knin were out already conducting the surveys.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you recall when the first report based on this instruction was produced?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The first reports based on this order were produced after it was given out in two or three days' time. So the provisional assessment was not based on this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up Exhibit P98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could -- could I ask some clarification from the witness. Mr. Anttila.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said earlier that the area where you found the shell impact was not any closer to any of the objectives, possible military objectives you identified later, than they were to the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I have great difficulties in understanding this in relation to your last marking, and I'm not talking about the F marking but about the M marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Marking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which if I compare that with the area where you found the shell impact seems to me if not closer than at JordBat's not further away from the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The thing is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I have difficulties to reconcile these two elements of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. I -- I, too, have that problem, because we were discussing this area being possible military target. I had not been there before Operation Storm, and to my -- to the best of my knowledge that area during the time that I spent there was in no way -- the marking M was in no way a military area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. And -- okay. Like I -- like I said, we had discussion about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I understand. Those objectives that you discussed to be possibly military targets were not included in your answer when you said that it was not closer to the northern barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, do you recognise this exhibit, P98?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yep, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And is -- was this report prepared pursuant to the instruction that you just saw on the screen?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes. This is what came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court who prepared this report?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I prepared this report with the numbers, can the columns, with the lines, but the information came from the different UNMO teams within the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Before we get to the basis for this report and where you received the information from, I want to first focus on the amount of damage which was reported in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please turn to the third page and focus on the first three entries where it's indicated on the left-hand side "Podkonje." And if we could move that over just a bit to get the numbers. A little bit more. A little bit more. Actually, I think we'll have to move out a bit so we can capture both the areas and the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you can follow along with me, Mr. Anttila. It indicates here that in Knin north-east, 41 houses totally damaged, 261 houses partially damaged. In Knin north-west 6 totally damaged, 94 partially damaged, and in Knin south-west 22 totally damaged, 236 partially damaged. And I'm going to hope my calculations are correct, I'm sure Your Honours would correct me if they're not, that would equal a total of 69 houses totally damaged and 591 houses partially damaged.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Making for total overall of 660 houses totally or partially damaged. Now, out of those 660 houses can you tell the Court an approximate percentage based on your observations of how many of those houses were damaged by shelling?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: It's very hard to say, but it's -- maybe I would say percentage maybe about 40 -- maybe 40 per cent of the houses were damaged due to shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And now getting back to this damage survey report and what it's actually based on, can you explain to the Court where the information that you entered onto this spreadsheet came from?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This information, all of it, came from different UNMO teams which conducted patrols within their AOR to -- to survey what was the damage done in the area. In certain areas where the UNMO team was placed on the Croatian side prior to Operation Storm you can see that there are damages reported that were assessed to be during the war or the fighting while -- while the so-called Krajina area was established, and the rest of it is -- is based on the information that came out from the teams based on the order to survey the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And how exactly did the UNMO teams convey this information to you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: It was conveyed -- basically the aim was to convey my daily sitreps and their special information packages that they gave in when they came for the team leaders meeting or something like that, when they arrived at the -- at the headquarters. So it was not released via electronical means in that way. It was physically taken into the headquarters with the paper sheets and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And to be clear, is -- did the information which was entered into this report by you, did that only come from UNMO team sitreps?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: It did not come only from UNMO sitreps. Like I said, it was hand-delivered or by other means, also electrical -- electrical with the floppy disk and things like that delivered to the -- to the headquarters and then compiled there by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up Exhibit P65.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking at Exhibit P65, can you tell us whether or not some of the UNMO teams used a form like this to convey the information to you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This is a form that was presented out to -- to be the basis on the information that should be delivered to -- to the headquarters about the different areas of where the damage was assessed. This particular report is just an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And did the UNMO teams on occasion use other means of communicating the information, any other kinds of reports or compilations of information?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Basically, yes. They did use different means by telling that, for example, compared to this report they would say that -- in their sitrep that row A such-and-such village, row B grid and then so on. So they could use this format even when reporting with their sitreps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And looking at this particular data collection form, you provided this to the OTP; right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This was provided by Sector South UNMO headquarters to the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I mean, you gave it to our office. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And with regard to the information which entered on this particular form, can you explain why some of the villages which appear at the top in the "Comments" field in row A, can you explain why some of these villages don't actually appear in the survey report which we look at earlier?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. Then -- then we are talking general area of Plavno, which is something that you can find on the map. Then you have different hamlets there which are Jovici, Stojakovici, and et cetera, which later on were compiled within a certain area, and a team had to make an assessment and a definition on which hamlets would be put under one name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you indicating that some of the hamlet names which appear --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. At this point I just object to the leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe -- Mr. Russo, would you to the best of your abilities refrain from leading. I don't know whether to what extent you were leading already, but if you rephrase your question certainly in a non-leading way, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please explain what you said just a second ago about the selection of areas to be reported? I'm not sure I understand that.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. You -- okay. It says -- in this particular report it says village name Plavno, and Plavno is an area where you have different groups of houses which in -- which are included in "Comments" column where it says: "Including Jovici," and et cetera. This is the general area of Plavno, and this is just information to record that we are talking about the hamlets of Jovici, Bajinac, Torbice, Grmuse, Stojakovici, et cetera, to have information that there might be some other hamlets that have not been visited yet. So just as well as the grid reference is a pretty rough one, that was at the time a way to keep track of which places were visited and which not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you then a question. "Et cetera" gives the possibility to identify [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. In this particular case these hamlets mentioned on the exhibit were visited and there could be some other hamlets in the general area of Plavno were not visited on that patrol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you didn't know which ones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We don't know which ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And getting back to the actual report, the spreadsheet that we looked at earlier, how many versions of that report did you prepare?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, it was updated. After it was created it was updated daily, on daily basis. Official reports that went out into UN archive, I think there were three versions of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were the subsequent versions, in your opinion, more accurate than the previous versions?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's the point of all -- all this work, that while the work proceeded the information was more accurate in terms of more villages being visited, more areas being covered and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And to your knowledge did the UNMO teams ever go back to a village that they had originally checked and recheck it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever ask any of them to go back and clarify some of the information that they gave to you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The information was constantly updated so that in a certain area the first visit would give out a certain report, and later on when the team would visit the same area again they would recheck the information that they gave out the first time, and if there was any change that change would be reported and then it would appear on the final report compiled by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at the -- the data collection form here, receiving a form like this where it indicates several villages -- or several hamlets inside of a general area and saying "et cetera," is that a level of specificity with which you were satisfied?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. This is a -- this is a preliminary report that -- in this particular case I recall that we gave the -- the team the order to be more specific on the hamlets that they have included in the -- in the report and so on. So later on that's why in the final version you cannot find all of these names, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could please pull up 65 ter 1587. If we could please turn to the second page of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking here at 65 ter number 1587, the date appears as 4/11/1995. Can you tell the Court whether or not this was the final report that you prepared?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is the last version that was submitted into a UN system as a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move for the admission of 65 ter 1587.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P176.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P176 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If, Madam Registrar, we could now pull up Exhibit P68.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, looking at Exhibit P68, can you tell me if you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This is a -- yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, please, who prepared this document.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This document was prepared by myself based on the daily sitreps coming from the teams to the Sector South UNMO headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court why this summary does not contain all of the information about the houses burned in the survey that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, this -- this is -- like I said, it's based on the daily sitreps. So this information is compiled from the information that was observed by the UNMO teams when they were on patrol. So if there was a house burning somewhere in the area, maybe the UNMOs were not present at that location at that time. So that's why in this -- this -- in this compilation of the sitreps you cannot find all the amount of houses being burnt, for example, that are in the -- in the list where you have the -- where -- when the teams were checking the -- the areas where -- where these happenings took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And you indicated that the information from here came from the UNMO sitreps. What -- what level of sitrep are we talking about? Can you explain that to the Court?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. First of all the teams would report to -- to UNMO headquarter in Sector South in this case, and then Sector South would report the significant happenings and findings to UNMO headquarter in Zagreb. That means that the information coming from the teams was not included in sitreps going to Zagreb, not all of it, only what was at that time, at that date, considered significant for the time being. So there are a lot of information that came out from -- from the teams that was not reported to UNMO headquarter Sector South or -- excuse me, I have to correct. That was not reported to UNMO headquarter in -- in Zagreb, rather than it was considered as general information and -- and with the reports given as a certain paragraph of, let's say, looting or -- or burning houses and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court which sitreps you pulled the information for this violation summary? Was it from the team level sitrep or from the HQ to Zagreb level?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. When this compilation of -- of -- like it said -- says, daily sitreps from 7 August to 4 September. This is the sitreps coming in from the teams to Sector South headquarters. So this information -- not all of this information can be found in the sitreps going to Zagreb. So everything -- or anything going to Zagreb was filtered from this information, and this information is not a compilation of everything that was in the sitreps. So it's only taking into account the matters that were supposed to be included in this type of report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you prepare --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, just for my understanding. In the last answer you said, "And this information is not a compilation of everything that was in the sitreps." When you said "this information," were you talking about the information that was sent to UNMO headquarters Zagreb, or were you talking about information we find in the summary of humanitarian violations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I was referring is that this report does not include all the information coming from the teams to Sector South UNMO headquarter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, did you prepare other kinds of reports in connection with humanitarian rights violations?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Other kinds. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, perhaps that was a --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't quite get the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What I'm trying to find out is if you participated in creating any additional reports with respect to human rights violations.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We -- officially we did not -- apart from these reports that are included here, we did not present any other official reports. Of course we had contacts with the other UN organisations, and on a verbal level we were discussing these matters, but official reports are included in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, can we please pull up 65 ter number 1586.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Looking at 65 ter 1586, Mr. Anttila, can you tell me if you recall this report?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Court what this report is based on? Where did the information come from?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, this is based on the information that we looked at previously. So it's based on the reports coming in from the teams about the damages and -- it's based on the same information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would move for the admission of 65 ter 1586.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Could I ask you one clarification. You said this was based on the same information. Did you mean based on the same information strictly speaking, or are you talking about the same source of information? I have not reviewed the document, so I do not know whether -- when it seems to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. This is based on the reports coming from the UNMO teams in the sector that -- the reports that we received in the headquarters, and this information coming from the teams included all the information based on which the compilation was done. So in that way I'm referring that it was based on the same information coming in as the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'm asking this for the following reason. If you make a compilation, you make a selection from the information that reaches you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, was it that this report was based on the same information that reached you, or was it based on the same selection of information that reached you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say that this could be a cover page for the -- for the -- for the compilation of information that was presented previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That sounds very much as rather the information -- the selected information for the other reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Russo, you're about -- you wanted to tender this. Mr. Kehoe said already he had no objections, speaking for all Defence teams. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P177.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P177 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, you can see in the "From" line here it indicates in addition to UNMO HQ Sector South, it indicates "Human Rights Activities Team (HRAT)." Were you part of a Human Rights Action Team?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Court basically how your responsibilities were divide between your UNMO tasks and the HRAT tasks?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. At that time in November myself, Major Peter Marti, and at the time Captain Ivan Valduranove from the Czech republic, we were part of the human rights team. Our task -- our main task was to compile the information given from the from the UNMO teams into these type of reports and to patrol together with the other UN organisations within the area. So we were not limited into the area of, let's say, Knin only. The area of the human rights team was the whole area of Sector South, and we would patrol in -- in groups of three people, which would include one person from UNCIVPOL, one person from UN Civilian Affairs, and then one person from -- from the military observing organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you share any of the information that you gathered about the UNMO damage survey, was any of that information shared with the HRAT team organisations or other organisations?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. There was -- at the time there was a human rights organisation in the UN organisation coming down all the way from at JordBat's the mission area level, but the actual fact was that the information that we had was available for the other participating parts of the human rights organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court who those other participating parts were?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, like I said, from my point of view at that time I was not very much concerned about -- okay. I was told that there was somebody from civilian affairs, from the UN organisation, coming to the patrol. For me at that time it was enough to know that civilian affairs, CIVPOL, and UNMOs were patrolling together. So I don't know exactly the organisational level or the positions that the persons were holding that were on the patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any meetings at which the information collected on humanitarian violations was discussed?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We were having daily briefings in the afternoon after having patrols, and in the daily briefings there was a specified representative of human rights team present in the sector. So sometimes it was myself, sometimes it was somebody from other UN organisations and so on. So -- and later on -- in the beginning it was more or less a task that we took up, and then later on it was passed over to CIVPOL and -- and UN civilian affairs to be responsible for reporting those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And were representatives from ECMM present at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Normally ECMM representatives would have access to -- to these daily briefings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand what "have access to" means. Did they attend?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: They attended when they were in -- in the location. When they were somewhere else they could not, of course, attend. But they were not restricted from attending the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Russo. We're close to the time where we usually have the break. I suggest that we have the break now. We will resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, from the fact that you're standing I deduce that you're the first one to cross-examine the witness. Mr. Russo, you're standing, as well, so you're not cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I have a minor matter not related to the cross-examination and I'll speak cryptically. During the break we attempted to provide the Court with a courtesy copy. I just wanted to make sure that was received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least as far as I'm concerned, you were successful. Yes. You were in every respect successful, Mr. Tieger. We'll try to deal with the matter today. Mr. Kehoe -- Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. I neglected to -- with respect to the very last exhibit which was admitted into evidence, that was P177, I neglected to have -- asked to have that admitted under seal as it contains the names of several of the victims discovered in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar -- I take it there are no objection against it being admitted under seal. Madam Registrar, P177 was admitted but is now admitted under seal. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Anttila. I would like to ask you some questions not only about what you talked about this morning but also develop some of the issues that came up during the course of your several written statements, okay? And I'll try to direct you to those statements as much as possible, and I do believe that you have written copies before you, but if you don't at any point please let us know. Okay?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, I think you noted for us, at JordBat's initially, that -- and this is in P171, in paragraph 1, that you were a construction or are a construction engineer.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's my -- I have been in college, and that's my civilian training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you also noted for us in that statement that you were not a professional military officer.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in Knin on the 14th of August, you had never been there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were unfamiliar with the area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That was my first time in that area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, before we go into what you talked about, at JordBat's initially on the provisional assessment and your testimony in that regard, I'd like to bring up on the screen Exhibit P60. And if we could go to the -- I guess it would be the third page of this. And, Mr. Anttila, that is the statement that you wrote on -- or was offered to the Trial Chamber on the 18th of December, 1995. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, tell us the circumstances of this. Where were you when this was written?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Where was I when this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me withdraw that. Who wrote it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You wrote it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where were you when you wrote it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who else was with you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: In that particular moment, I was asked to make a statement about the crater analysis that we performed, and at that moment in the office where I physically wrote it was nobody else present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you type it up?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I typed it up myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you sign it at that time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I signed it at that time, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who asked you to prepare this?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This question was brought up by the -- by the Tribunal investigator. I think it was the Danish -- what's his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me help you there. Would that have been Joakim Robertson?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, was he present when you were typing this up?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you went through the information, for instance, and got the grid references, et cetera, did you go to a map or did you have that information with you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Of course I had the map on the wall in the office where I was working at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you examined it at the time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, I was -- I was looking at the map, and the -- yeah. The grid reference is a general area where -- like it says here it's -- it's a four-digit grid reference, which means that it's not pinpointing things out. It's, rather, giving the area where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the four-digit grid reference is one kilometre by one kilometre, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when did Mr. Munkelien sign this?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That I don't have information on. I don't know when he signed it. He was not there at the moment when he -- when he -- when he -- I did not see him signing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, this particular document, had you talked to Mr. Munkelien about this before you prepared it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We talked about this incident. We talked about the crater analysis after we conducted the actual analysis individually, both of us, and at that time we came to the conclusion that this was what was -- had taken place, that the findings were the same, that we both came to the same conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now, when you -- I mean, did you sign this? I think your cover sheet says that you signed it on the 18th of December, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I ask one clarify question. I'm not a native speaker, Mr. Anttila. Neither are you, but we conducted the actual analysis individually, both of us. Do I have to understand that you analysed the crater and Mr. Munkelien did analyse the crater, that you came to your own conclusions and then found out that you shared the same --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same conclusion. So you did not come together to a conclusion in a conversation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But each separately came to this conclusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went there. He went there. There was six impacts. He was studying the three on that side. I was studying the three on that side, and we met in the middle, and we had reached the same conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I may -- by the way, this piece of paper is on the Sector South letterhead. Sector South letterhead didn't exist at this time, did it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Sector South was terminated before that time, but we did not have any other basis to use at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, we've had a lot of information about Sector South ending, and I just wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, you noted for us in your statement and I refer to the December 2007 statement, 172, at -- excuse me. That would be 173, at paragraph 6, that you had had artillery training as well as the crater analysis training with the Finnish armed forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is correct. I'm -- I'm trained to be the mortar or artillery firer, aiming position in my military training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And obviously prior to that -- when you were conducting that training and you were being instructed, you were taught that when you do this type of analysis it's important to be as precise as possible, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, normally. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And by the way, when -- before you went to Sector South, had you had training in HV weaponry as well as ARSK weaponry?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We were given information about the -- the weaponry normally used in -- or available for the parties in this area, which were the weaponry that was available for JNA prior to all this happened and then what was -- what was brought in later on. So we had a book or a booklet -- rather, a book where all the weapons were described, and we had several different types of -- of ways of defining what the weapon used would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I may, sir -- if I might have one moment. So it would be accurate to say that most of the training that you received was on weaponry that had been used by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: It was not specified as to be used by JNA. It was general information about the weaponry available in this area, and it was -- it was not based on JNA information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you noted for us when you went through this statement -- or prior to this statement you and Mr. Munkelien were in the same area and examined the impact area and then came together and came -- and drafted this particular memo or voluntary statement that we have in P60. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. Well, that -- like it says in the cover sheet, that was drafted on the 18th of December, which is far beyond the time when we actually were on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And -- but it was consistent with the conclusions that you made back on the -- I guess the 17th --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: 17th of August, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me bring up 1D19 -- or, before I do that, I mean, you note that the grid reference here is WJ9778; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we bring up 1D190034. And, Madam Registrar, we'd like to show this to the Court via Sanction. If I can just move to -- if I can just change that to 0035 first. Now, if you can take a look at this, Mr. Anttila, and I direct your attention to the upper right-hand corner which has the grid reference of 9778.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that -- you have to say --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I can see the grid reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me take you down to the other grid which is 9677, and in the small red circle, that's the approximate area that you told us was the impact area for these -- these rockets, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the grid -- was the grid reference that you put in your report of December the 18th incorrect?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This is correct. The grid reference is incorrect. I agree with you with that. So -- and the reason for that was that at the time when making this statement we did not have the maps available with the -- such specific grids where you could determine exactly the point where you had been. And like I said, it's more or less to give the general area which we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, in the area that's 9778 is the area where the hospital is, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you told us during direct examination that when you went back and reported to Mr. -- or Colonel Hjertnes --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- you pointed to the area on a map?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that map was on a wall?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that map had grid references, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I may, sir, let me turn your attention to M -- excuse me, P70.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I will offer 1D190035 into evidence before we move to P70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D166, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D166 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have P70.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, Mr. Munkelien testified here on the 15th of April. On page 1502, lines 12 to 14, Mr. Munkelien was asked by Mr. Russo to locate the area where he conducted the crater analysis and place an A next to it. And you see the location where the A is located on the left-hand side of this exhibit, don't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah. I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, that location is different, quite different, from the location that you selected, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And both locations, if we can, and let's turn our attention to 1D190034.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, again, if we could show this to the Court via Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I have taken the liberty of circling the area at the top where Mr. Munkelien circled.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Neither one of the locations that you and Mr. Munkelien circled is in grid 9778, are they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: You are correct there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when this comes to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, at this time I will offer 1D190034 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D167, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D167 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, you would agree with me that when rendering a decision on fire being directed towards a military target, having the precise location of those impacts is crucial, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn our attention, if you will, to the actual weaponry involved. You note here that it's an M-63 128. And I'm reading from P60, by the way. That's your exhibit. And you note that -- at the middle of the page that the patrol was able to recover one body of a rocket from an impact hole and was able, therefore, to determine definitely the calibre of the weapon used.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you determined the calibre by measuring the bottom of the particular piece that was recovered, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you came to the conclusion based on that that it was a 128-millimetre, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I can turn your attention to -- let me, if I can pull this, and I can bring up Exhibit D83.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is that D83? I think that's P83, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you previously told the Office of the Prosecutor that this is one of the shells that you recovered from the area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you also noted in your statement that -- and this is P173 -- by the way, who are the individuals in this photograph? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: This is Major Scott from Canada and Major Simon Coley from UK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm referring to P173, paragraph 8. You note -- if you can turn to that. That's the December 2007 statement, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you said that: "In our report we mentioned that rocket shells were fired from the direction of 20 degrees north by north-east. I do not have any photographs or notes to confirm the assessment, although at the time we made notes." By the way, did you take photographs at the time?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the notes that you made, where are they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: They were in a -- in a scrapbook, which was later on destroyed or -- you know, I don't have it any more. So it's not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you note that the directions can be determined by the markings within the crater.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I.e., the fins and the detonator make certain markings with the crater. Now, as you can see from the document that's on -- excuse me. The photograph that's on the screen, the shell that you had did in fact have fins on it, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. This is -- when we talk about fins, we are not talking about actual fins of the ordnance which is exploding. We're talking about the impact area where -- when the detonator detonates the rocket, the artillery shell, or a mortar grenade, it creates a certain type of impact area, and in that area you can see the fins, which I refer to in this document.
