This particular -- or this particular rocket, there were something wrong with this one because it did not explode the way it was supposed to be. You're not supposed to find a rocket shell like that after it has impacted the area where it's hitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, we will go into that in one moment. I mean, you did note in your P173 statement at paragraph 3 that with regard to this incident that -- and this is the last line: "Major Munkelien is better placed to provide more detailed explanation of the analysis than myself." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, in that respect that Major Munkelien has or had at that time, been on several UM missions before, and as a military observer, for myself at that time that was the first time as I was acting as a military observer within the former Yugoslavia area in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did he also have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we are talking about fins, you still now say that in that area you can see the fins. Are we talking about stabiliser fins and what do you mean by --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We're not talking about any physical fins. We are talking about markings on the ground. So if I draw a picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are both not native speakers, but I think you call that a swatch. Is that -- that is a current --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Splash.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Splash or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Splash nor -- but that has several parts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are -- okay. When the ordnance hits the ground then there are typical markings on the ground based on which type of artillery weapon is used, whether it's a mortar, whether it's a cannon, whether it's a rocket, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's sure that's most important for me at this moment is we are not talking about stabiliser fins being found --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or leaving any marks. It's rather the shape of the impact that you find on the ground.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Impact that you can find on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By way of clarity, when you talk about fins you're talking about the impact on the ground?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But let's look at what you said in your statement at paragraph 8 at 173 -- at P173. You note that the direction can be determined by the markings within the crater, i.e., the fins and the detonator make certain markings within the crater.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you -- when you were talking about fins on that issue, you were talking about the stabilise be fins --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I asked this question to the witness a second ago, and he clearly answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But fins are not physical things but are forms or shapes of the impact on the ground. So fins, of course, I have to look in the dictionary, but it may have different meanings and otherwise we have to understand on the basis of the testimony of the witness that the way in which he expresses himself in English on this respect would not be hundred per cent. We find some other examples of that in the statement as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I was just taking the witness back to at that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then you put the same question as I had put already to him and which he answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go back to the photograph that was on the screen, and if we could blow-up the bottom portion of that, please, if we can, if it doesn't blur.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, taking a look at this do you see the markings that are -- well, there's one looking directly at the photograph. Do you see that in the bottom portion of the shell?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I do see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And that was a stabilising fin for the 128, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't get the point here. I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is still confusion now as far as markings are concerned. Could you please be specific on your question? Perhaps we could use --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could use the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The usher will certainly assist you and perhaps then using the cursor in a particular way that you can precisely tell the witness what the markings were that you included in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Madam Usher. On the shell -- could you go to the bottom portion with the marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not to be marked. We should use the cursor here, rather, so let's take out this -- yes, and now could we just move the cursor or even that thing. We just had to remove other things. The tiny little circle can be used. Yes. Now we have the cursor there. Mr. Kehoe, please guide the usher and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Just take that cursor up just a little bit. To that line. No, no. Just within the same general there. No, where you were before. Just over to the right just a bit, and you see that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that line, sir, where it's pointing to?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah, just barely. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That particular line was where the fin for the 128 had been that broke off, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us turn our attention, sir, to this particular shell, if we can. You note in your statement that this is a 128.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I could go to Defence Exhibit 83. I'm sorry. It is 85. I'm sorry. I apologise. Now, you told us that you measured the bottom of the ground to determine -- to definitely determine what the calibre was; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: On which statement that is stated?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you look at P60.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your statement. And you don't say the measuring, but you noted that you definitely determined the calibre.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Exactly. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you determine the calibre by measuring the bottom of the rocket across?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge and what I can remember, that's the way it was done, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, did you have training on the -- and I believe the M-63 128; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Excuse me, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have -- you had training with regard to the M-63 128?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I have not been trained to use this kind of a multiple-rocket launcher. No, Finnish army does not have these kinds of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you trained as to the characteristics of the M-63 128?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, during my UNMO training.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I turn your attention to the map -- excuse me, the exhibit that's on the screen. Do you recognise this as the M-63 128 shell?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know where the propulsion system is in this weapon?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The propulsion system is in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this particular 128 M-63 does not have any wings on it for stabilisation, does it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if the shell that you recovered on the 17th of August, 1995, with Mr. Munkelien had wings on it, then the shell that you recovered was not from an M-63 128, was it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Like I said before, I could agree with you that you could barely see some markings on the shell that we recovered. I don't know if there were any fins attached to that ordnance when this came out, and I cannot determine whether that marking was made by something that was attached to that part or if it was made by something else hitting on the side of the -- of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My simple question, Mr. Anttila, was if that shell had wings, stabilisation wings, it was not an M-63 128, was it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. We don't know if it had it. I'm not speculating on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, that's what happened if you say if this had happened that would be the consequence. It's a matter of logic. I'm counting superfluous and -- questions. I'm above ten, now, so would you please. I could mention them, but I -- you were done the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, I'm trying to take the witness through it as logically as possible so the witness can follow through. I understand, Your Honour, that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's your logic and the witness in the last two questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- had to correct you twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I understand that. I'm just trying to take the witness through it as logically as possible and as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm saying that you're --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not trying to -- [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore I count and ten -- and that's got nothing to do with logic. I mean, it's about -- whether he was a construction engineer. That so clearly appears from his statement. What's the use to ask him again? There are -- that's in evidence. Well, I could give you questions like whether he was taught to be as precise as possible. We're all always be taught to be as precise as possible. I mean, these are really superfluous questions. Please proceed. We waste even more time if we continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must take issue with the last one because the witness said that the grid reference that he gave was an approximation. I mean, that was the point on that. So I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you think that is because he was taught to be unprecise or is it just that he was unprecise, which clearly appears from the other questions which are very interesting. Please proceed. And the answers. Questions and answers, the others ones are very interesting. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, that's refreshing, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, sir -- now, sir, when you recovered this particular weapon, you went back, did you not, to a book that you had received that allowed for recognition of the M-63, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I could bring up on the screen D84.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that the book, sir? You can look at the next page if we may?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. Well, the cover looks like the one I have with me still.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could just spin that. And that appears to be the entry in there with regard to the M-63?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, did you examine any other weapon systems in that book concerning 128s other than the M-63? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall. Of course when it was clear to us that it was a rocket impact, we looked at the rocket launchers and so on. So -- anyway, I don't recall during that time to have specifically examined all the contents of the book, but we -- and I went through the rocket launchers where from I made the conclusion that it would be M-63.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could bring up 1D0015, and paper copies have been distributed. 1D190015. If we could put that on the ELMO if we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, this is a photograph from the same book, and turning to the next page, this book notes the weapon system of an M-77. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that is likewise a 128?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you instructed during or prior to going down to that the JNA had these weapon systems in their arsenals?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I had the information that they -- this could be available within the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'll offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D168 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could put D86 on the screen. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, are you familiar with this weapons system?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I have seen it in the pictures. I have never come across physically with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I might have the assistance of the usher. If we could just put the ELMO down. I think it's a little difficult for the witness to see me. If I can -- we are done with the ELMO at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We go to -- I'm sorry. If we can go to D85. And by the way, with regard to the M-77, were you aware that the army of the Serb Krajina had the M-77?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I would -- objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I just want to clarify. The witness was shown two different documents, both indicating an M-77. One is an M-77 YMRL; the other is the M-77 Ogani. I'm not sure if the question refers to one or other of those, or if he's asking if they're the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm just asking generally if he knows if they had an M-77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if there are several times of M-77, then of course we would have to find out and if there are relevant differences between the two of them in respect of what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Colour might not be the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had the information this this M-77 could be available within the area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just turn to D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir -- and if we could just highlight that just a bit. During the course of your training and being instructed on the M-63 as well as the M-77, were you made aware of the differences in the shells?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We were not trained on a specific details of each type of rocket that would exist in different types of weaponry. We're trained on the calibre determination and things like that, how to determine the different impacts of the different types of weapons. But particular details of each weapon were not, of course, conducted in the training that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, just taking that one step further and going to the photograph that's on the screen, the photograph on the bottom, do you recognise that as an M-63 shell?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look at the photograph on the top and we look at the longer shell, do you recognise that as an M-77 shell?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: As far as I understand, that should be an M-77, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the M-77 shell, if we look towards the back -- excuse me, to the right-hand side of that photograph, that particular shell has the stabilising wings to it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, it seems to have them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go back to D83. Now, looking at the shell that you took from the ground and looking at how it collapsed after impact, as you sit here today, sir, does that appear to be an M-63 shell or an M-77 shell?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To my understanding it should be an M-63.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And tell us what happens to an individual rocket on impact. What -- how much of it is destroyed on impact and how much remains?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, normally you cannot find any remains of the rocket after the impact. That's what happened with the other impacts of the rocket. When it explodes properly, you cannot find at the impact zone these kind of remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And during the course of your training were you instructed that after impact -- during the course of your training were you instructed that the length of the impact -- excuse me, that the length of the original site after the impact, after the impact now, the length that's remaining is approximately one-third the size of the original shell? Were you taught that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To answer your specific question, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we went through the mathematics of the length of the M-77 and how much would remain as opposed to the M-63 on how much would remain after impact, you wouldn't have any idea about that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's not what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just explain to me, then.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The shell that is in the picture is something that comes from an ordnance that did not explode properly. Normally you would not find this kind of a -- if the explosion happens the way it's supposed to happen, you will not find this kind of an ordnance in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you also noted for us, and I'm going back to P60, that the approximate angle of fire was 20 degrees north by north-east.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if I may put 1D190011 on the screen, and if I can just do this via Sanction, Madam Usher. Now, Mr. Anttila, looking at this particular map and taking the location from the area of impact and going 20 degrees, it points towards the area of Strmica, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, sir, let me ask you, when you went through this did you do any examination or any questioning as to who was doing the shelling on the 4th and the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Which parties -- what party was doing the shelling?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Did I do any examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ask?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Ask? Who? Who could I have asked?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, just to take your question, sir, were there UNMOs that had been present during the 4th and the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Okay. Now -- okay. So prior to that, and I'm still standing with the statement that I -- that I made at that time is that we observed on the ground that these impacts came from this direction, and I did not have any discussion about who should or would have been the actual shooter in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So you have no idea who actually shot this --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. I was just looking at the impacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go to D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I will offer 1D19011 into evidence. 0011 excuse me into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D169.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D169, which, by the way, does not appear on the screen. Yes. D169 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just if we can go to D89. Now, if we go to page 4, paragraph 2. Now, if we can just bring that up a little bit and just go down a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can look at that paragraph. You see at about 051500 hours. Do you see that, Mr. Anttila?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it notes that ARSK soldiers of unknown strength were seen occupying defensive positions in general area of Strmica a with a grid reference. Tanks and mortars were seen at the same positions. At 051815 they fired 12 rounds of artillery from Strmica towards Knin." Were you aware of this, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. This is the first time I see this document and this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you were travelling around and trying to find out houses that were damaged, houses that were hit by shelling, did you ask anybody back at UNMO Sector South headquarters who was doing the shelling in this area?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I did not interrogate the UNMOs in that respect. I did not ask them these types of questions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me just direct yourself quickly to D120. If I may just scroll up just a bit. And the third paragraph down, and this is an article from the Toronto Star of the 5th of August. It notes that: "The Croats are very close." There's a quote by then Colonel Leslie. "Croats are very close. Tanks are returning fire right outside our compound and artillery is impacting inside Knin." During -- again more specifically with this particular comment did you interrogate the -- not interrogate, just ask. Not the course of interrogation. Just ask the UNMOs about --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I did not have any information about this. This is the first time I see this kind of document, and I did not have information about Colonel Leslie's comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we can go back to your particular map, which is 174. Now, the -- if I can just pull that up. Now, A being the area that you examined, but the areas that you said that the -- that the other members of Team Podkonje examined were B, C, and D.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just to give us a reference, I mean, you weren't a team leader on Team Podkonje, were you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You were just one of the members?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I was one of the members who had been given a special task by the SMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now -- and the team leader was a Felix --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: At that time it was Felix Anglada.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the areas that we look at here, B, C, and D, they are most heavily populated areas in Knin, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And based on that, if we can turn to P64. P64. And could we blow that up, and paragraph 1. Now, it notes -- if we could just blow that up a little bit more in paragraph 1. It notes in paragraph 1 that the "UNMO Team Podkonje has made a provisional assessment of the damages caused by the HV ops, 04-06 August '95 in the town of Knin. The report is based on a rundown of 70 per cent of the Knin town and gives a brief overview of the situation." Now, the 70 per cent of the Knin town was the residential areas that you just picked out in your chart, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's what -- I had pointed out that those areas were the areas where these patrols went into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on that, if we go to -- to 2: "In general, shelling was concentrated against military objectives. The damages caused by the shelling to civilian establishments is concentrate to close vicinity of military objectives." And then it notes "only few impacts is observed in the other urban areas." Now, correct me if I'm wrong, but the conclusion that was made at the time was that after looking at areas where most of the people lived that the conclusion of Colonel Hjertnes was that all -- the fire was basically directed towards military targets. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The document speaks for itself, and it indicates that the damage is to the close vicinity of military targets. It doesn't make the conclusion Mr. Kehoe has referenced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, this was number 11. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you gave a statement in January of 1996, you noted that you agreed with that assessment totally, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Then when you changed your opinion, did you learn about what the military targets were?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The thing is that this statement and -- and this report is made on the 18th of August, 1995, and things did not stop from happening on the 18th of August. There were further things that happened later on, and also at that time with the experience that I had from the area I could agree with this statement, but later on I learned more about the area and other things also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let's take what you learned. Did you learn about particular facilities and as to whether or not they had been used by the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I still have -- we had this discussion with -- with the team members and the headquarters staff whether a certain location was used by RSK or not, but at that time I did not have this information. The only military objective at that time that I knew of was the north barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't know, sir, for instance, I think on the Senjak barracks, whether or not it was used militarily or not, do you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The particular -- let me go back to your chart. If we can go back to 174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, may I ask some clarification from the witness in the following respect: You said, "This report is made on the 18th of August, and things did not stop from happening on the 18th of August." That is a rather unclear answer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you. Did you suggest that any of the damage caused by shelling could have resulted from shelling after the 18th of August --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or was it things to be happened is what you learned and what you observed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we talk about things happening after the 18th of August, that was clearly something that was not caused by shelling. It was -- it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but what --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we are talking about looting and burning and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that seems to be a rather separate issue --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- from what we find in this document, so it's a bit of unclear --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Yeah. On the 18th when the teams went out, not all the things were cleared out, and you could not access all the roads within these areas, and then later on when you went into -- deeper into that area rather than just driving through them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you're not talking about the town of Knin at this moment, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Outside Knin -- inside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Inside Knin, for example, the areas which have been pointed out, you could not go to all the roads because there was debris on the road, and when this was cleared then you could find there were some impacts of shelling and later on, so not all the information was available on the 18th. That's the point that I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand what you meant by other events happening.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, it's important to -- when making a decision whether or not something is a military target, it's important to know whether or not it's being used for military purposes at the time --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is something that normally -- yeah, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So let us go to P74. Excuse me. I'm sorry. P174. Mr. Anttila's map. I apologise. P174. Now, the area that you circled did not include in the area that you had some question about and must be in the next document, which is I believe P175. I'm searching for the document where you circled the barracks. Yeah. This one. Now, the area that you had, P175, and you have noted with an M --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- as opposed to the F with the factory, that was the area that you had some question about, correct?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to D161, page 6. Now, that area you had as M is known as the Senjak barracks, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Senjak barracks for me as a name is not familiar, because we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just turning our attention --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: -- we did not use that name for that area at the time when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could turn to page 6. Page 6 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The pages are a bit confusing here, Mr. Kehoe. On the bottom we find 6 out of 10. On the top we find 3, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm perplexed, as well, Judge, because of course I don't read Croatian or B/C/S. If I can just get a reference from my colleague. I do believe, Judge, it is the 1820, or the 1620. If you can see that designation on the right-hand side. Do you see that, Judge? Okay. If you see the 1620. If you almost go straight across to the 1620 in the B/C/S. Up on the top. Higher, higher. 1620. Higher. Yeah. And if we go across at the -- at the -- into the B/C/S, it likewise has a 1620.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just get the date reference on the prior page, on 5 of 10. And if -- by way of reference, Your Honour, this is the -- this is the -- the diary of the chief logistics of the RSK. And if we note the date at the top, 2 is dealing with the attack on 4 August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we can flip to the next page. And if we can scroll that up. It notes "at 1620 hours I went to the PMK rear command post Senjak barracks, had a short meeting with senior officers and deployed them as follows," then gave a list of individual officers.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I understand that you don't know that was called the Senjak barracks, but would you agree looking at that that this facility described in this document, this barracks described in the document on the screen would in fact be a military facility?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The document doesn't seem to indicate what facility. I mean, it indicates a Senjak barracks. I don't see how that relates to a picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to clearly distinguish between what the witness can tell us and what his exegesis is of documents. Sometimes counsel are even better than witnesses in exegetic exercises, and whether or not the Chamber is good at that is still to be seen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Looking at this screen, Mr. Anttila, would you agree with me that the officer in charge is at the Senjak barracks giving instruction to other officers?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to the Senjak barracks, the area that you noted in P175 -- go to P175. P175. The area that we have circled as an M -- which you circled as an M, what information did you receive that suggested that that facility was not a military facility?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: On the date -- on the 17th, I did not have any information about that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you did your examination, did you go back to UNMO headquarters and ask people at Sector South headquarters what that facility was?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No, I did not. I went back, and when we performed the crater analysis, we did the analysis on spot. We went back to the headquarters. We gave the information in, and I had -- I did not have any information about the area of -- which has been marked with M to be a military objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, Colonel Hjertnes had been in the area long before you got there, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And to the extent that you were giving him the information, were you relying on his superior knowledge in the area on the 17th of August, 1995, to make decisions concerning targets or non-targets, which could be military targets or non-military targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well, at that time I was -- I was deployed there, and I was serving under his command. So I would expect that he would have more information and more basis for making judgements and such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, then, you noted for us in this provisional assessment that Colonel Hjertnes got this information from various people on Team Podkonje, right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were people in Team Podkonje examining some of these locations prior to the 17th to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Or do you know?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't have any information about whether they were on patrol, but I would -- that's all making assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I see. So you don't know.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So -- but you do know that he was the central repository for that information.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And based on that information, he then filed the provisional assessment.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: To my understanding that's the way it worked, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you knew about the provisional assessment at the time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I knew about it, that he was giving the information further on to the system, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that had been sent up the -- to Zagreb as well.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes, I would expect also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did you ultimately learn that -- if I could just take a look briefly at P90 -- D90. Excuse me. Now, sir, this is a United Nations Security Council report of the 23rd of August, report of the Secretary-General, and if we could move to paragraph 5, page 2, first sentence. And in that particular line it says that: "On 4 August, 1995, the Croatian army launched the attack in sectors north and south and Knin fell on 5 August following concentrated shelling." Now, you know of no report issued by the Secretary-General which noted that there was any type of indiscriminate shelling on Knin, do you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's number 14, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was not there at that time, so I don't have any information about this time. I arrived on the mission area on the 4th of August. I stayed in Zagreb until the 14th and so on, so I don't have any information about this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you don't know of any other UN report by the Secretary-General after that, do you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. I'm not that much familiar with the Secretary-General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the final report, in P64 it notes that the survey continues to get a more accurate picture and better assessment. Detailed report to follow within a week.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you informed that Colonel Hjertnes has informed the Prosecutor that I recall that Team Podkonje - he's talking about the final report - "Team Podkonje's report was consistent with the provisional assessment. I do not recall anyone voicing a different opinion." Have you been told that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted during the course of your testimony that you believe, looking at the figures presented by counsel, that 660 houses were destroyed, and you noted that 40 per cent were by shelling.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's a rough figure that was -- it's an estimate. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you make that determination, that is without a full knowledge of the military targets that were in Knin, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That number, 660, is later number from the 18th of August. It's coming in November, and then by that time there was a lot more information that I had gathered from the area than on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question is this, sir: You noted that 660 houses were either damaged or destroyed --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's in November. That's the number in November. We are not talking about the same number as in the report on the 17th or 18th of August. 18th of August was a brief overview, and in November when we are talking about 660 houses, then we are talking about the thorough investigation or assessment which has been made during that time with several patrols in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, there are two issues. The one is additional knowledge in November compared to August as far as damage or destroyed houses is concerned. That's one. The second element of this question is whether you gained additional knowledge about potential military targets between August and November. Your answer is about the damage, apparently, whereas Mr. Kehoe apparently seeks to find out whether you had any additional knowledge about potential military targets gained between August and November. Could you -- so you have dealt with the first part to some extent. Could you please deal with the second element of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So I -- I received some information from -- from the UNMOs within the sector about the fact that, for example, in that area marked with M could be a military target in that sense, yes. So -- so I gained more information about possible military targets that would have been there in the area before the Operation Storm, after the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to Mr. Kehoe to find out what level of detail you gained additional information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can you tell us the level of detail that you got and who you --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We went driving past the area, and then, okay, we stayed the -- the house where I was staying at was on the road going out past this area marked with M, and while we were driving past that, for example, Tchernetsky was telling me that, okay, there used to be some RSK guys over there prior to Operation Storm, but it was never very specific information about whether it was a barracks or if it was just something that they were staying at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But isn't it true that we are still talking about this one piece of -- on the map which was marked with an M, did you gain any knowledge about logistical centres, about communication centres? Did you gain any information apart from that specific spot, what was identified, I think, by the Defence as the Senjak barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from that spot, I don't -- I could not tell you where the RSK was keeping their troops, where they had their compounds, other than north barracks, and then I have a suspicion that with the -- within the area which is marked with M there could have been some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. At the same time, by giving this explanation, it appears that you have a rather limited conception of what a military objective could be, that is, troops being there. That's the reason why I asked for the other matters like logistical centres, communication centres, transport issues, government-related offices in relation to the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when I'm referring to military objectives, and we are talking about military being involved in those objectivities. So I did not consider at that time, for example, the railway station to be a military objective, even though I can understand that you could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- consider one like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can take you back, if I -- for one moment, based on your answer, to P63. If we can blow up the top of that, and if we go into the "Classifying the damage on buildings," do you see that sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it notes "Classify damage of buildings as follows. 1 not damaged. 2 minor damage (looted with broken windows and doors)." And for some reason the numbers are transposed. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that, Your Honour? It's a 3 and a 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that. That's logic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 2. Is damaged. Roof, floor, and construction. Under that, Factories and official buildings are not to be included. Now, did that indicate to you that Colonel Hjertnes had assessed factories and official buildings to be legitimate targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I did not think about that at that time in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you inquire to anybody why we're not looking at factories and official buildings?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, what -- what did you think that a -- when you read this, what did you think that official buildings were?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Official buildings would be administration buildings where the authorities would have their offices and, like, police stations and government buildings and stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So did you examine them during the course of -- of your survey throughout Knin?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: We did not survey those buildings specifically, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, do you know where they were?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I -- I knew that they were along the road where we -- we knew the places where they were in -- in -- in downtown Knin, but during the investigation or the patrol on the 17th, when we went out to do the crater analysis, which is the provisional assessment, we were not looking for that area. We were going through the -- just driving past the area, and this order has been issued out while we were on patrol on the 17th. So this was not information that we would have had while we were going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's bring up P175 again. P175.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I mark on this, I mean, do I make another exhibit? How do ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Usually if there is any additional marking where this exhibit is admitted into evidence, then it should get a new number, although it could be on the basis of this already-marked exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sir, where the police station? If you could mark it.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. I don't recall the exact location, but I would put it round about there. In this area of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we're using a blue pen, which is reserved for the Prosecution. Therefore, if we could take it out and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I believe the red is for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The red is for the Prosecution. Yes. Yes, you're right. I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And were you informed where the former headquarters were for the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you informed of facilities where officers and staff of the ARSK had resided?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you -- other than the F location, were you made aware of any other factory facilities that were targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there a police station in the area where you were patrolling on the 17th of August? The area that you -- if we go back to the map, it would be 174. If we can go back to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll move this particular document into evidence, and we can go back to P174.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit D170.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D170 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The area that you were patrolling in A, which you said where you did the impacts.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was there a police station there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't have any recollection of seeing a police station there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about around C? Was there a police station there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't know because I was not patrolling through that area at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us just address ourselves back to your statement concerning the damage. You said that 660 facilities in Knin were damaged and 40 per cent by shelling. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is a statement that I have compiled from the reports coming from the UNMO teams, so it's not observed by myself. It's -- it's a compilation of the reports from the teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we look to P66. This is your document that was previously discussed during direct examination, and if we could go to -- the page number is -- six pages in. It should be 548207.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The -- and I think this is just a misunderstanding. The document which was shown to him on direct examination was a later version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise. Well, this is the 4/11/1995 one that was put in -- placed in evidence previously as P66, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's either try to avoid confusion on different versions of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Hmm?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Judge. I thought we were looking at this from November 4th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is now proven as such. I mean, whatever is in evidence you can put to a witness, but I think if you want to test the accuracy of the final result of an exercise, then better use the last version. If there is any intermediate period you would like to examine in detail, then of course you could use another version, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think this version is exactly the same, Judge, so if I could just -- on this particular score turn to this particular page, and it is one that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the other one? Then I'll check -- I'll find the other one. The newest version, Mr. Russo, is?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe -- I'm sorry. I believe that was moved in as 176, P176.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P176. I'll get it on my screen so we can confirm. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. If I just get -- what is the date on 176, counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I believe the one which was admitted today was the 4/11/95, and I think P66 may be the 4 October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, P66 is dated 4/11/1995. If we look at the first page of P66, it's dated 4/11/1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'll have to check which one was admitted this afternoon was what was -- 65 ter number 1587. I'm sorry. I'm not trying to create confusion. I just want to make sure there we're talking all about the same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see is the number you just gave, Mr. Russo, page 176 has as its date 4th of 11, 1995. So if you check the other one to see what is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I hope this helps and doesn't -- I'm looking at it on e-court, that is P66, and I have a heading data on population left in Sector South in destroyed houses after OP storm 4/10/1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So 176 now is 4/11. Please proceed on the basis of the most recent version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually, the document that I'm dealing with 4/11/1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's P176.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm going to go into this in some detail. I don't know if this is a good time for a break, Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it would be, but let me just check one other thing. Yes. This is a good moment for a break, but we'll first ask Mr. Anttila to follow the usher, to leave the courtroom so that we have a second for a small procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the Defence parties give me any indication about time still needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am the only person that's going to cross, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may -- depending on what happens, I may have 15 minutes at most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Nothing arises from the Cermak Defence team at the moment, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kehoe, how much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe that certainly the balance of today, Judge, and maybe about an hour tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that at JordBat's one thing is for sure, that we'll finish with this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by tomorrow. Yes. That was my only matter of concern at this moment. We'll have a break and resume at five minutes to 1.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by tomorrow. Yes. That was my only matter of concern at this moment. We'll have a break and we'll resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Anttila, welcome back.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can look back at P176 and turn to 5 -- page 548207. And just below that ... Now, if you could just orient -- can you see that, Mr. Anttila? I know that's a little tough, but if we could just look at that line about halfway down. I do believe this is the listing that Mr. Russo was talking to you about, and if you see the Knin north-east, north-west, south-west, and if we take those numbers over to the right and you count the numbers up of the 41, 622, which comes to 69, and the 251, 94, 236 that comes to 591, the 591 and the 69 or 660, is that the methodology you employed?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the total number would be those numbers added up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it's your testimony that 40 per cent of those, some 240, were destroyed during Storm -- or excuse me there was shell damage from Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah. That would be the assessment, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to the front page of this document, which is -- this is P176, 00548202. And you have a column that notes, and this is one, two, three, four -- five over, "Population after 4 August." Now, this is -- if I am correct, this is the population in these villages that were there after the end of Operation Storm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is the names that had been recorded by the UNMOs in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As being in those villages after Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And I see that you have here that the title of this document is "Data on population left in Sector South and destroyed houses after Operation Storm."

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's what it reads there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where in this document -- and if I may, if this document is dated to destroyed houses after Operation Storm, where is there a designation or is there a designation in this document as to houses that were damaged or destroyed during Storm?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: There is no designation about whether the houses were destroyed during the Operation Storm. So basically what -- what it says here, that -- that is what could be found on the ground when doing the survey at a certain time in these villages and hamlets and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You noted for us on direct that 40 per cent of the houses were damaged or destroyed as a result of shelling.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That was in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In Knin. And -- so that's approximately from the number of 660, approximately 260.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Where is the itemisation of those houses that were either damaged or destroyed as a result of shelling? Where is that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you make a decision about whether or not -- well, I can just withdraw that. By the way, are you familiar with the concept of dual-use targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't understand the -- the phrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand. I mean, it's -- I realise that English is not your first language and I speak quickly. And by the way anytime you don't understand anything I say, please --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The concept of dual-use targets, are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the concept of mobile targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And truck -- military trucks and mechanised units you would put in military targets?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when assessing type of damage as a result of shell-fire, for instance, it's important to know, for instance, if there were mobile targets in the area, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah. It's -- it would be important to assess the aim of the fire. Doing the surveys like this afterwards, it's not possible to determine whether that area -- area you had any mobile targets in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to this document, you -- and I'm talking about P176, if we could go to the last page. Now, just looking at these numbers, you note that there are 22.213 buildings, 863 totally damaged and -- excuse me, 8.063 totally damaged, and 9.207 partially damaged in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I know the rough math of that is that 78 per cent of the buildings in Sector South were either destroyed or damaged. Is that your assessment?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The assessment is that out of the 22.000 buildings checked, this number of buildings were destroyed. This does not include all the buildings in the Sector South. There is more buildings than 22.000 buildings that sector, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So there is yet a -- so you decided to include some buildings in and not include others?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. This includes the villages and the hamlets that have been visited by UNMO teams doing this survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that there are other villages and hamlets that haven't been visited, that are not part of this?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: There is a possibility that not all the hamlets and villages within the sector would have been visited by UNMO teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, how do we know whether or not a village was visited or not?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Each team kept a record of -- of the villages in their area of responsibility which they visited, and it was their responsibility to -- to cover the area as well as possible during the time period given to the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. And when they told you about a village you wrote it down here.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Of course they would give a report that, okay, they have visited this village and such-and-such things were found out there. So that's how this report and the lines in the -- in the -- in this report came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go -- let's go to P65 and talk a little bit about your answer. Now, P65 is the document that you discussed on direct examination that had a listing of villages in the Plavno Valley.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look at those, Jovici, Bajinac, Torbice, Grmuse, Stojakovici, and now it says "et cetera." That was supposed to give you an idea of the villages that they saw; right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That was supposed to give me an idea of the amount of work that they have done. What was important to me when I was putting up these reports was that in the general area of Plavno they had visited these certain hamlets and not all of these hamlets appear on the -- on the list because, okay, like I said before, this is an example of the document that was sent in, and this particular document we went back to the team saying that you have to be more specific on which hamlets you have been visiting, but, okay, in general this is the basis for the information that was given to compile this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's go back to P76. P176, excuse me. 176. Page 548207. Now, we note if you look in the Plavno Valley notations that there is a Grmuse listed. And if we go to the following page there is a Stojakovici listed as well as a Torbice, but no Jovici or Bajinac. Isn't that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So if we look at this, there is no reflection that these particular villages were in fact visited, does it?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: There is no reflection of those hamlets being visited, and they are included in later reports in other hamlet names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. Anttila, but if you look at this document, you wouldn't know that they had visited those little hamlets, would you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: From this document I would not know that. Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if you look at these numbers that were in the Plavno Valley by these villages that were damaged by storm or minor damage -- excuse me, damaged or totally damaged from P65, the numbers don't match up with the numbers that you have set forth for these villages, does it? And let's just look at -- you have 207 residences totally damaged or minor damaged, and if we can look at the villages in Grmuse, there is no partial damage, no total damage, no buildings whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Can I have the previous page, please where the Grmuse is appearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. I apologise. I'm looking at -- in Grmuse?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is no report of any total damage or any partial damage; right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And we go to the following page and we look at Stojakovici and Torbice -- I apologise it's Stojakovici. We have five totally damaged and five partially damaged. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And for Torbice we have no damage and no buildings. Well, it's no buildings but no damage.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the document P65, if we can go back to that. I'm sorry, P65. That reflects 263 buildings in the villages and 207 -- it says, "Damaged believed due to Operation Storm." So the numbers that you have in November don't match what is in this particular document, do they?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: No. And that is because like I said before this is an example of a report where we went back and we asked for additional information, and we did not put into the reports that we filed in information that was in a way that we interpreted it inaccurate or did the not -- okay. 207 does not appear there. It could have been included there if we would have been not trying to be precise. So what this particular report caused was that the team was given information that this is not enough or accurate enough to put into the report so we will not include this information in the report, and that's why the number of damaged buildings does not appear on the final report on the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when we take the 207 damaged buildings from Operation Storm in P65, when your report came out, that was reduced -- and if we go back to P176, page 548207, and again we look at Grmuse that's got no partially damaged and no partially damaged. And if we go to the next page and we look at Stojakovici and Torbice, we see that the only insert on damages in Stojakovici which is five totally damaged and five partially damaged.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So we look at the village damage that we can ascertain. When we look at those villages, we have reduced the number of partial or total damage from the report you received of 207 to 10.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That is what we could report, that we can confirm. Originally the damage seen in that area was in 207, and we said to the team that, Okay, you have been going out there doing the survey, but this is not accurate enough. So you need to be more specific when you do this report. And that's why it looks like from -- from this -- this report that they never gave in a specific report about Torbice, for example, about the buildings and so on later on. So we did not include anything that would be something that we could not determine specifically, you know, that could be observed and confirmed later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: But we tried to be as specific as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So who -- who's reviewing the work of this team that was going out there to do this?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: The team leader, of course. And then the teams were sending out patrols. Patrols were tasked to go into a hamlet, to review the village, to make a report, and then that report was submitted into the sector headquarters where I would receive it, and then the human rights team would make an assessment on -- if the information; for example, in this particular case when we are talking about the example of the report, that was not specific enough to be included as it was in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And just taking what you're saying, I believe you said on direct examination that you have just back at Sector South headquarters gathering this material from the teams; right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I was not visiting all these villages. I was there getting the information and putting it together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you received this P65, this -- this report from Team Podkonje --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- you concluded that this information was inaccurate, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Because -- yes, I concluded that the information was not accurate enough. I did not conclude it inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Anttila, you give us this P65. Where are the rest of these records that were filled out by these teams?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: These records were kept in the headquarter Sector South, and when the -- when Sector South was terminated, then they were handed in into a UN headquarters in Zagreb, in -- actually in Pleso. We took all the files to -- to a container. That's how much I know about that, because they -- that's where we were assigned to take the files to have somebody to take them over with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what happened to them afterwards and so on. I don't have them with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the -- you also collected this information in P68. If we can bring that screen up. Now, this is -- this is a document that you put together, I take it.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the three ones that I have submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, is it your testimony, sir, that the information concerning burnings was not included in situation reports that was sent up to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: My conclusion is that not all of the information that came from the teams was included in sitreps going to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me -- let me change that just for a second. Was information concerning burnings included in sitreps that were being sent to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: You cannot answer that question yes or no. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You're welcome to explain, sir.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Okay. The information coming from the teams was included in the sitrep when the operations officer saw it as important to the situation at the moment. So we got information from the teams about burning and looting coming in which was not reported to Zagreb at a certain time. Sometimes that was when it was going on on a larger scale. Then it was something that would be reported as a -- as part of the sitrep as an example in a way. I don't know if I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out from this sitrep. You would agree with me that there are literally scores of instances in these reports that you put together in P68 with a situation report that had been sent to Zagreb discussing house that is were burning and houses that had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Right? You have to say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you are saying to me that the information sometimes was sent to Zagreb concerning burning and sometimes it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's why we -- in the organisation we have the operations officer to make the assessment which part of the information is important to be reported up -- upwards in the -- in the organisation. If we would have included all the things coming from the -- from the teams, the sitreps to Zagreb would have been huge. And that is the job of the operations officer to make the assessment what will be reported and what will not. So the reports to Zagreb do not include all the information coming in from the teams to the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you do realise that Zagreb was relying on the information that had -- you were presenting to them to make decisions not only about the UN mission in the former Yugoslavia but also information that had been passed back to New York?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And is it your testimony here that all of the possible human rights violations as it pertains to burnings, for instance, wasn't given to them on a routine basis?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: It's the same thing as it is with, let's say, if there is a case of shelling you don't report all the impacts. You report the shelling. And the same thing happened here. So not every single piece of information coming from the teams was sent to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, there was a difference after you received the order from Steinar Hjertnes to go out and do this damage assessment. There was a difference in the format of the sitreps, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, prior to the 17th there was no humanitarian --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Aspect, inspection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- aspect to the sitrep; right?

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And after that there was an entire separate section of the situation report that had do to with the --

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- humanitarian area. And that was the information that was sent up.

utterances.speaker: KARI ANTTILA
utterances.text: Yes. Again, that is a matter of how you put up a sitrep. You compile the information that you gather within the area and then you report it as it -- either by incidents or -- the other way is to -- to report as a general information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
